record.paper_title: Control theory of stochastic distributed parameter systems: recent progress and open problems
record.original_question: For semilinear stochastic distributed parameter systems, especially stochastic parabolic and stochastic hyperbolic equations, can one prove controllability results analogous to those known for deterministic semilinear distributed parameter systems, including cases where the nonlinearity grows more slowly than s log(s)^(3/2), and can one identify further classes of nonlinear terms for which controllability still holds?

evidence.quote: (5) Controllability for semilinear SDPSs. In [9], based on sharp estimates on the dependence of controls for the underlying linear equation perturbed by a potential and fixed point arguments, it was proved that semilinear parabolic and hyperbolic equations are null controllable with nonlinearities that grow slower than s log(s)^{3/2}. Whether such results can be obtained for semilinear stochastic parabolic/hyperbolic equations is open. On the other hand, for nonlinearities growing at infinity as s log(s)^p with p > 2, one cannot get the null controllability due to the blow-up of solutions. However, this does not exclude controllability for some particular classes of nonlinear terms (e.g., [7]). More generally, there are lots of interesting results for controllability of semilinear distributed parameter systems (e.g., [6]). So a systematic study of controllability problems for semilinear SDPSs deserves attention.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider semilinear stochastic distributed parameter systems on a bounded smooth domain $G\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ over a finite time horizon $(0,T)$, driven by a one-dimensional standard Brownian motion $\{W(t)\}_{t\ge 0}$ on a complete filtered probability space $(\Omega,\mathcal{F},\{\mathcal{F}_t\}_{t\ge 0},\mathbb{P})$. Two model classes are of interest:

(A) The semilinear stochastic parabolic equation
$$
\begin{cases}
 dy - \Delta y\,dt = \bigl[f(y) + \chi_{G_0} u\bigr]dt + \bigl[g(y) + v\bigr] dW(t) & \text{in } (0,T)\times G,\\
 y = 0 & \text{on } (0,T)\times \partial G,\\
 y(0)=y_0 & \text{in } G,
\end{cases}
$$
where $G_0 \subset G$ is a nonempty open control region, $u$ and $v$ are $\{\mathcal{F}_t\}$-adapted square-integrable controls, and $f,g:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ are locally Lipschitz nonlinearities.

(B) The semilinear stochastic hyperbolic equation
$$
\begin{cases}
 dy_t - \Delta y\,dt = \bigl[f(y,\nabla y, y_t) + \chi_{G_0} u\bigr]dt + \bigl[g(y) + v\bigr] dW(t) & \text{in } (0,T)\times G,\\
 y = 0 & \text{on } (0,T)\times \partial G,\\
 y(0)=y_0,\ y_t(0)=y_1 & \text{in } G,
\end{cases}
$$
with analogous control and adaptedness conventions.

A system is said to be globally null controllable in time $T$ if for every admissible initial datum there exist adapted controls $(u,v)$ steering the state to zero almost surely at time $T$.

Solve the following:

(i) Prove (or disprove) that, in analogy with the deterministic theory, the systems in (A) and (B) are globally null controllable whenever the nonlinearities $f$ (and $g$) satisfy the asymptotic growth condition
$$ \limsup_{|s|\to\infty} \frac{|f(s)|}{|s|\,\log^{3/2}(1+|s|)} = 0. $$

(ii) Identify further classes of nonlinearities $f,g$ growing faster than $s\log^{3/2}(s)$ at infinity for which null (or approximate) controllability of (A) or (B) still holds.
artifact.status_search_result: Global null-controllability of stochastic semilinear parabolic equations has been established for globally Lipschitz nonlinearities (e.g., the Annales IHP/EMS Press paper "Global null-controllability for stochastic semilinear parabolic equations") and for semi-discrete versions, using refined Carleman estimates and fixed-point methods. However, the general superlinear case with growth up to $s\log^{3/2}(s)$ — and the corresponding stochastic hyperbolic case — appear to remain open, since standard compactness arguments used in the deterministic Fursikov–Imanuvilov–Zuazua approach fail in the stochastic setting. Identifying broader classes of admissible nonlinearities is also unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Global null-controllability for stochastic semilinear parabolic equations
status_evidence.snippet: Global null controllability of forward stochastic semilinear parabolic equations with globally Lipschitz nonlinearities is established via refined Carleman estimates and Banach fixed point theorem.
status_evidence.claim: The Lipschitz case for stochastic semilinear parabolic equations is solved, but the superlinear log-growth case is not addressed.

status_evidence.title: Null controllability for semi-discrete stochastic semilinear parabolic equations
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2025) work treats semi-discrete stochastic semilinear parabolic equations under Lipschitz-type nonlinearities; the continuous superlinear case remains delicate due to the failure of compactness in stochastic functional spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Active research continues on stochastic semilinear parabolic controllability; the s log^{3/2}(s) growth threshold has not been reached.
